purpose: Positive control with a trade-off. design.movements: through only: N->S, E->W, S->N, W->E; one approach lane per arm

expectation.kind: assumed (analytical; computed from the design only, before any simulation)
expectation.method: Webster (1958) green split at the baseline's cycle; clearances unchanged

formula.flow_ratio: y_i = max over the approaches served in phase i of q_a / (n_lanes_a * s)
formula.optimum_cycle: C0 = (1.5 L + 5) / (1 - Y), with Y = sum_i y_i
formula.displayed_green: G_i = g_i - I + l (with l = I, as assumed here, G_i = g_i)
formula.whole_seconds: largest remainder, keeping sum_i G_i = C - n_phases * I; a phase below the minimum green gets the minimum and the others share the rest in proportion
formula.delay_for_predictions_only: Webster (1958): d = C(1-lam)^2 / (2(1-lam*x)) + x^2/(2q(1-x)) - 0.65 (C/q^2)^(1/3) x^(2+5 lam), lam = G/C, x = q/(s*lam), q and s in veh/s
formula.queues_for_predictions_only: mean queue (veh) = q*d (Little's law); queue at the end of red (veh) = q*r with red r = C - G

assumptions: saturation flow s = 1800 veh/h per lane (textbook base value, not calibrated against SUMO). Every approach has the same lanes, so s cancels out of the split; it matters for the optimum cycle and the degrees of saturation (see sensitivity)
lost time per phase l = 5 s, equal to the intergreen (yellow 3 s + all-red 2 s): start-up loss and use of the yellow assumed to cancel, so effective green = displayed green
cycle kept at the baseline's 70 s
yellow, all-red and phase order unchanged
through movements only; no turning, pedestrian or lane-utilisation factors

mirror.rule: 2 * bad - correction; if outside the validator's limits, scaled down to the maximum green and cycle keeping the split, then whole seconds with the minimum green

baseline.kind: simulated (validity checks only; program and demand are assumed)

limitations: SYNTHETIC known-answer test of the evaluation and selection stage (positive and negative controls). The junction, its demand, its signal plans and every candidate are written in code; no proposer runs (Muse is not exercised), so this is not a test of discovery. It says nothing about the real NGSIM Lankershim intersection 2 baseline, or about any real junction.

Report text written for counted demand does not apply to this designed demand: the clip length ('Counts come from a 3600 s clip; flow intervals are wide'), the note on stop-line discharge counts, and the Poisson 95% flow interval shown for each movement describe counting vehicles in a clip. Here the flows are designed, so those intervals carry no information.
The bundle's instruction to a model ('state expected effects in words, not numbers') does not apply: no model was asked; every candidate was written by code from the pre-registration.
The analytical Webster model is not calibrated against SUMO (saturation flow assumed); it only labels expected directions.
The small random perturbations change a deliberately bad plan by up to 5 s per green; they are not nulls. The exact null is rejected by the validator before simulation, so no simulated null exists.

In the baseline the queue was censored on arm E (vehicles held off at entry on seeds 6, 8, 17), arm S (vehicles held off at entry on seed 2), so those arms' queue claims are untestable for every candidate (lower bounds).

false_positives.definition: a Holm-confirmed improvement (any candidate, any improvement metric) whose pre-registered analytical change for that metric has the opposite sign, i.e. is predicted > 0 (worse) by any amount. The reference is an uncalibrated Webster model (see model_agreement), so a count here is a disagreement with that model, not proof of a spurious result
false_positives.opportunities_definition: tested improvement claims (p-value computed) whose predicted change is > 0: the claims that would be false positives if confirmed
false_positives.rule_of_three_note: 3/n when 0 of n; it treats the claims as independent, which they are not (they share the baseline runs)

model_agreement.note: verdicts against an uncalibrated Webster model (assumed saturation flow): agree = improves/better, worsens/worse or inconclusive/about unchanged

outcome.conclusion: [reallocation] Known-answer test of the evaluation and selection stage (no proposer runs; Muse is not exercised). Positive control: the pre-registered correction I5 (greens {'EW': 40, 'NS': 20} s) was NOT selected (I5 worsens max_queue_m.N, max_queue_m.S, mean_queue_m.N, mean_queue_m.S); its Holm-confirmed improvements: mean_delay_s, mean_queue_m.W. Negative controls: the exact null I7 was rejected by the validator before simulation and not selected; the mirror I12 was simulated (incomplete) and not selected. Of 8 small perturbations of the bad plan (not nulls), 1 had a Holm-confirmed improvement and 8 worsened at least one metric. False positives (a confirmed improvement contradicting the pre-registered direction of an uncalibrated Webster model, which agreed with 65 of 96 predicted comparisons, 68%, and was opposite in 0): 0 of 16 confirmable claims predicted worse (rule-of-three 95% upper bound 0.19). In the baseline the queue was censored on arm E (vehicles held off at entry on seeds 6, 8, 17), arm S (vehicles held off at entry on seed 2), so those arms' queue claims are untestable for every candidate (lower bounds).
